::: {.question-box}
How do I stop copy-pasting the same helper functions into every analysis?
:::

## The idea

Every project needed the same little helpers. So I collected them into two proper packages,
both called **rushtools**: one for R and one for Python, living side by side in one repository.

::: {.card-grid}
::: {.cute-card}
[📦]{.icon .bg-blush}

### R package

`R/`, `tests/` and a `DESCRIPTION` file, tested with **testthat** via `devtools::test()`.
:::
::: {.cute-card}
[🐍]{.icon .bg-sky}

### Python package

Modern `src/` layout with `pyproject.toml`, tested with **pytest**.
:::
::: {.cute-card}
[✅]{.icon .bg-butter}

### Automatic checks

Two **GitHub Actions** run every test on each push, so a broken function shows up as a red ✗.
:::
:::

## Install

```r
# R
remotes::install_github("halireena/rushtools", subdir = "r")
```

```bash
# Python
pip install "git+https://github.com/halireena/rushtools#subdirectory=python"
```

## What I learned

::: {.learned}
- How R and Python packaging work, and how similar they are underneath.
- Writing tests first makes refactoring much less scary.
- Continuous integration catches mistakes I would never notice by hand.
:::
